//! Rich diagnostic error types for the akh-medu engine.
//!
//! Each subsystem defines its own error type with miette `#[diagnostic]` derives,
//! providing error codes, help text, and source chains so users know exactly what
//! went wrong and how to fix it.

use miette::Diagnostic;
use thiserror::Error;

/// Top-level error type for the akh-medu engine.
///
/// Each variant wraps a subsystem-specific error, preserving the full diagnostic
/// chain (error codes, help text, source spans) through to the user.
#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]
pub enum AkhError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Vsa(#[from] VsaError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Store(#[from] StoreError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Graph(#[from] GraphError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Symbol(#[from] SymbolError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Infer(#[from] InferError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Reason(#[from] ReasonError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Skill(#[from] SkillError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Provenance(#[from] ProvenanceError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Pipeline(#[from] PipelineError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Engine(#[from] EngineError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Agent(#[from] crate::agent::error::AgentError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Autonomous(#[from] crate::autonomous::error::AutonomousError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Glyph(#[from] crate::glyph::GlyphError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Grammar(#[from] crate::grammar::error::GrammarError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Dispatch(#[from] crate::dispatch::DispatchError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Compartment(#[from] crate::compartment::CompartmentError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Library(#[from] crate::library::LibraryError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Workspace(#[from] crate::workspace::WorkspaceError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    RuleMacro(#[from] crate::rule_macro::RuleMacroError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Temporal(#[from] crate::temporal::TemporalError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Arity(#[from] crate::graph::arity::ArityError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Contradiction(#[from] crate::graph::contradiction::ContradictionError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Skolem(#[from] crate::skolem::SkolemError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Cwa(#[from] crate::compartment::cwa::CwaError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    SecondOrder(#[from] crate::reason::second_order::SecondOrderError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Nart(#[from] crate::graph::nart::NartError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    ResourceDiscovery(#[from] crate::bootstrap::resources::ResourceDiscoveryError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Ingestion(#[from] crate::bootstrap::ingest::IngestionError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Competence(#[from] crate::bootstrap::competence::CompetenceError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Orchestrator(#[from] crate::bootstrap::orchestrator::OrchestratorError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Audit(#[from] crate::audit::AuditError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Nlu(#[from] crate::nlu::error::NluError),
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// VSA errors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]
pub enum VsaError {
    #[error("dimension mismatch: expected {expected}, got {actual}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::vsa::dim_mismatch),
        help(
            "All hypervectors in an operation must share the same dimension. \
             Check that you created them with the same Dimension parameter, \
             or re-encode the mismatched vector."
        )
    )]
    DimensionMismatch { expected: usize, actual: usize },

    #[error("hypervector not found for symbol {symbol_id}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::vsa::not_found),
        help(
            "The symbol has no associated hypervector in item memory. \
             Either insert it first with `item_memory.get_or_create()`, \
             or check that the symbol ID is correct."
        )
    )]
    HypervectorNotFound { symbol_id: u64 },

    #[error("empty bundle: cannot bundle zero hypervectors")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::vsa::empty_bundle),
        help("Provide at least one hypervector to the bundle operation.")
    )]
    EmptyBundle,

    #[error("encoding {encoding} is not supported for this operation")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::vsa::unsupported_encoding),
        help(
            "This operation requires a different encoding. \
             Bipolar supports bind/bundle/permute. \
             FHRR and SSP will be available in a future release."
        )
    )]
    UnsupportedEncoding { encoding: String },

    #[error("HNSW index error: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::vsa::hnsw_error),
        help("The HNSW approximate nearest-neighbor index encountered an internal error.")
    )]
    HnswError { message: String },
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Store errors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]
pub enum StoreError {
    #[error("I/O error: {source}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::store::io),
        help(
            "A filesystem operation failed. Check that the data directory exists, \
             has correct permissions, and that the disk is not full."
        )
    )]
    Io {
        #[source]
        source: std::io::Error,
    },

    #[error("redb transaction error: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::store::redb),
        help(
            "The embedded database encountered a transaction error. \
             This may indicate corruption — try running with a fresh data directory. \
             If the problem persists, file a bug report."
        )
    )]
    Redb { message: String },

    #[error("serialization error: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::store::serde),
        help(
            "Failed to serialize or deserialize data. \
             This usually means the stored data format has changed between versions. \
             Try re-ingesting your data."
        )
    )]
    Serialization { message: String },

    #[error("key not found: {key}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::store::not_found),
        help("The requested key does not exist in the store. Verify the key is correct.")
    )]
    NotFound { key: String },

    #[error("memory map error: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::store::mmap),
        help(
            "Failed to create or access a memory-mapped file. \
             Check available virtual memory and file permissions."
        )
    )]
    Mmap { message: String },
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Graph errors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]
pub enum GraphError {
    #[error("node not found: symbol {symbol_id}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::graph::node_not_found),
        help(
            "The symbol has no corresponding node in the knowledge graph. \
             Insert a triple containing this symbol first."
        )
    )]
    NodeNotFound { symbol_id: u64 },

    #[error("duplicate triple: ({subject}, {predicate}, {object})")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::graph::duplicate_triple),
        help("This exact triple already exists in the graph. No action needed.")
    )]
    DuplicateTriple {
        subject: u64,
        predicate: u64,
        object: u64,
    },

    #[error("SPARQL query error: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::graph::sparql),
        help(
            "The SPARQL query failed. Check the query syntax and ensure \
             the oxigraph store is initialized."
        )
    )]
    Sparql { message: String },

    #[error("traversal depth exceeded maximum of {max_depth}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::graph::depth_exceeded),
        help(
            "The graph traversal reached the maximum allowed depth. \
             Increase `max_depth` if deeper traversal is needed, \
             or check for cycles in your graph."
        )
    )]
    DepthExceeded { max_depth: usize },

    #[error("analytics error: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::graph::analytics),
        help("The graph analytics computation failed. Check that the graph is non-empty.")
    )]
    Analytics { message: String },
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Symbol errors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]
pub enum SymbolError {
    #[error("symbol allocator exhausted: cannot allocate more than u64::MAX symbols")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::symbol::exhausted),
        help(
            "The symbol ID space is exhausted. This is extremely unlikely \
             in practice (requires 2^64 allocations). If you see this error, \
             something is very wrong — check for ID allocation loops."
        )
    )]
    AllocatorExhausted,

    #[error("invalid symbol kind: {kind}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::symbol::invalid_kind),
        help("Valid symbol kinds are: Entity, Relation, Composite, Glyph.")
    )]
    InvalidKind { kind: String },

    #[error("symbol not found: id {symbol_id}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::symbol::not_found),
        help("No symbol exists with this ID. Use `all_symbols()` to list available symbols.")
    )]
    NotFound { symbol_id: u64 },

    #[error("duplicate label: \"{label}\" already registered as sym:{existing_id}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::symbol::duplicate_label),
        help(
            "A symbol with this label already exists. Use `lookup_symbol(\"{label}\")` to retrieve it, \
             or choose a different label."
        )
    )]
    DuplicateLabel { label: String, existing_id: u64 },

    #[error("symbol not found by label: \"{label}\"")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::symbol::label_not_found),
        help(
            "No symbol with this label exists. Lookup is case-insensitive. \
             Create the symbol first with `create_symbol()`."
        )
    )]
    LabelNotFound { label: String },
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Inference errors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]
pub enum InferError {
    #[error("no seeds provided for inference query")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::infer::no_seeds),
        help("An inference query requires at least one seed symbol to start from.")
    )]
    NoSeeds,

    #[error("inference depth exceeded maximum of {max_depth}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::infer::depth_exceeded),
        help(
            "Multi-step inference reached the depth limit. \
             Increase `max_depth` in InferenceQuery or simplify the query."
        )
    )]
    DepthExceeded { max_depth: usize },

    #[error("no activations produced from {seed_count} seed(s) at depth {depth}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::infer::no_activations),
        help(
            "The seed symbols had no outgoing edges in the knowledge graph. \
             Add triples connecting these symbols, or increase `max_depth` to \
             explore further."
        )
    )]
    NoActivations { seed_count: usize, depth: usize },

    #[error("analogy requires exactly 3 distinct symbols, got {count}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::infer::invalid_analogy),
        help(
            "Analogy inference computes A:B :: C:? — provide exactly three \
             distinct SymbolIds (a, b, c) to find the fourth."
        )
    )]
    InvalidAnalogy { count: usize },

    #[error("activation for {symbol_id} below threshold: {confidence:.4} < {threshold:.4}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::infer::below_threshold),
        help(
            "The recovered symbol's confidence is too low to be considered a \
             valid inference. Lower `min_confidence` or `min_similarity` in the \
             query, or add more supporting triples to the knowledge graph."
        )
    )]
    BelowThreshold {
        symbol_id: u64,
        confidence: f32,
        threshold: f32,
    },

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Vsa(#[from] VsaError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Graph(#[from] GraphError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Reason(#[from] ReasonError),
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]
pub enum ReasonError {

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Provenance errors

#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]
pub enum ProvenanceError {
    #[error("provenance record not found: id {id}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::provenance::not_found),
        help(
            "No provenance record exists with this ID. \
             Check that the ID is correct, or query by derived symbol instead."
        )
    )]
    NotFound { id: u64 },

    #[error("provenance ledger requires persistence — no durable store configured")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::provenance::no_persistence),
        help(
            "The provenance ledger needs a data directory for storage. \
             Pass --data-dir to enable persistence, or use Engine::new() \
             with a configured data_dir."
        )
    )]
    NoPersistence,

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Store(#[from] StoreError),
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Pipeline errors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]
pub enum PipelineError {
    #[error("pipeline {name} has no stages")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::pipeline::empty),
        help("A pipeline must contain at least one stage. Add stages before running.")
    )]
    EmptyPipeline { name: String },

    #[error("stage {stage_name} execution failed: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::pipeline::stage_execution),
        help("An individual pipeline stage encountered an error during execution.")
    )]
    StageExecution { stage_name: String, message: String },

    #[error("pipeline {pipeline_name} failed at stage {stage_index} ({stage_name})")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::pipeline::stage_failure),
        help(
            "A pipeline stage failed. Check the inner error for details. \
             The pipeline was aborted at this stage."
        )
    )]
    StageFailure {
        pipeline_name: String,
        stage_name: String,
        stage_index: usize,
        #[source]
        source: Box<PipelineError>,
    },

    #[error("stage {stage_name} expected {expected} data, got {actual}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::pipeline::incompatible_data),
        help(
            "The output of the previous stage is not compatible with this stage's input. \
             Check pipeline stage ordering — e.g. Retrieve produces Traversal data, \
             not Seeds."
        )
    )]
    IncompatibleData {
        stage_name: String,
        expected: String,
        actual: String,
    },

    #[error("no seed symbols available for pipeline execution")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::pipeline::no_seeds),
        help("The pipeline needs seed symbols to start. Provide initial Seeds data.")
    )]
    NoSeeds,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Engine errors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]
pub enum EngineError {
    #[error("invalid configuration: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::engine::invalid_config),
        help("Check the EngineConfig fields. {message}")
    )]
    InvalidConfig { message: String },

    #[error("data directory error: {path}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::engine::data_dir),
        help(
            "The data directory could not be accessed. \
             Ensure the path exists and has read/write permissions."
        )
    )]
    DataDir { path: String },

    #[error("ingest format error: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::engine::ingest_format),
        help(
            "Triple data must be in one of these formats:\n  \
             Label-based: {{\"subject\": \"Sun\", \"predicate\": \"is-a\", \"object\": \"Star\"}}\n  \
             Numeric: {{\"s\": 1, \"p\": 2, \"o\": 3}}"
        )
    )]
    IngestFormat { message: String },

    #[error("contradiction detected: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(akh::engine::contradiction_rejected),
        help(
            "The triple was rejected because it contradicts existing knowledge \
             and the engine's contradiction policy is set to Reject. \
             Use ContradictionPolicy::Warn to insert anyway, or \
             ContradictionPolicy::Replace to overwrite the existing triple."
        )
    )]
    ContradictionRejected { message: String },
}

/// Convenience alias for functions returning akh-medu results.
pub type AkhResult<T> = std::result::Result<T, AkhError>;

/// Result type for provenance operations.
pub type ProvenanceResult<T> = std::result::Result<T, ProvenanceError>;

/// Result type for pipeline operations.
pub type PipelineResult<T> = std::result::Result<T, PipelineError>;

/// Result type for skill operations.
pub type SkillResult<T> = std::result::Result<T, SkillError>;

/// Result type for audit operations.
pub type AuditResult<T> = std::result::Result<T, crate::audit::AuditError>;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn vsa_error_converts_to_akh_error() {
        let err = VsaError::DimensionMismatch {
            expected: 10_000,
            actual: 5_000,
        };
        let akh: AkhError = err.into();
        assert!(matches!(
            akh,
            AkhError::Vsa(VsaError::DimensionMismatch { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn store_error_converts_to_akh_error() {
        let err = StoreError::NotFound { key: "test".into() };
        let akh: AkhError = err.into();
        assert!(matches!(akh, AkhError::Store(StoreError::NotFound { .. })));
    }

    #[test]
    fn infer_error_wraps_vsa_error() {
        let vsa_err = VsaError::EmptyBundle;
        let infer_err: InferError = vsa_err.into();
        assert!(matches!(infer_err, InferError::Vsa(VsaError::EmptyBundle)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn error_display_messages_are_descriptive() {
        let err = VsaError::DimensionMismatch {
            expected: 10_000,
            actual: 5_000,
        };
        let msg = format!("{err}");
        assert!(msg.contains("10000"));
        assert!(msg.contains("5000"));
    }
}

name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  # Scoped to the seshat crate — the full akh-medu workspace release build
  # OOM-kills rustc on the Solstice runner. Broader test/clippy/release-build
  # coverage can return once the codebase is lighter or the runner is bigger.
  check-seshat:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config protobuf-compiler libprotobuf-dev libssl-dev

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: |
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain stable
          echo '. "$HOME/.cargo/env"' >> ~/.profile

      - name: cargo check -p seshat
        run: |
          . "$HOME/.cargo/env"
          # Default features only (includes `embedding`; excludes the memory-
          # heavy `synthesis` candle feature which OOMs the runner).
          CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo check -p seshat

  docker-seshd:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    # Intentionally independent of check-seshat so that one doesn't block the
    # other. The docker build itself catches anything check missed.
    #
    # Auth: Solstice's workflow-runner writes /home/sol/.docker/config.json
    # at VM boot from repo secrets in priority order
    #   REGISTRY_TOKEN > PACKAGES_TOKEN > FORGEJO_TOKEN > GITHUB_TOKEN
    # with username from REGISTRY_USERNAME (default "token", which Forgejo's
    # registry rejects on POST). Required repo secrets for push to succeed:
    #   REGISTRY_TOKEN     = a Forgejo PAT with scope: write:package
    #   REGISTRY_USERNAME  = toasterson
    # Both live at .../toasterson/akh-medu/settings/actions/secrets.
    # We deliberately do NOT add an explicit `docker login` step here:
    # Solstice's auto-auth runs before any step, and an explicit login step
    # would just overwrite ~/.docker/config.json with whatever raw string
    # we give it (Solstice doesn't yet substitute ${{ secrets.X }} inside
    # step env: blocks — only in runs-on).
    #
    # Branch detection lives in `.forgejo/scripts/resolve-branch.sh` — it's
    # called inline in each step that needs $BRANCH because $GITHUB_ENV
    # isn't reliably set on Solstice (an earlier `echo BRANCH=... >> "$GITHUB_ENV"`
    # crashed dash with `ambiguous redirect` and silently killed the job).
    steps:
      - name: Build seshd image
        # Always runs — PRs need to catch Dockerfile regressions. On
        # main/develop the image gets an additional branch-named tag ready
        # for the push step.
        run: |
          set -eu
          REGISTRY=code.aopc.cloud/toasterson
          SHA=${SOLSTICE_COMMIT_SHA:-${GITHUB_SHA:-local}}
          SHORT_SHA=$(printf '%s' "$SHA" | cut -c1-12)
          BRANCH=$(sh .forgejo/scripts/resolve-branch.sh)
          echo "detected branch: '$BRANCH'"
          TAGS="-t $REGISTRY/seshd:$SHORT_SHA"
          case "$BRANCH" in
            main|develop)
              TAGS="$TAGS -t $REGISTRY/seshd:$BRANCH"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "building with tags: $TAGS"
          docker build -f docker/seshd.Dockerfile $TAGS .

      - name: Smoke-test seshd binary (catch stub-binary regression)
        run: |
          set -eu
          REGISTRY=code.aopc.cloud/toasterson
          SHA=${SOLSTICE_COMMIT_SHA:-${GITHUB_SHA:-local}}
          SHORT_SHA=$(printf '%s' "$SHA" | cut -c1-12)
          SMOKE=$(docker run --rm --entrypoint seshd "$REGISTRY/seshd:$SHORT_SHA" /nonexistent 2>&1 || true)
          echo "smoke output: $SMOKE"
          if [ -z "$SMOKE" ]; then
            echo "seshd produced no output for a missing config - likely stub binary" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Push seshd image
        # Two pushes, two different gates:
        #
        #   * SHORT_SHA tag — always pushed, because downstream (the flux
        #     HelmRelease) pins to this to get reproducible deploys. It's
        #     the tag that actually matters.
        #
        #   * branch tag (`:main` / `:develop`) — only pushed when we can
        #     confidently identify the branch. Resolving in-script means we
        #     don't depend on `github.*` expression support (inconsistent on
        #     Solstice) and don't die on the empty-branch case.
        #
        run: |
          set -eu
          REGISTRY=code.aopc.cloud/toasterson
          SHA=${SOLSTICE_COMMIT_SHA:-${GITHUB_SHA:-local}}
          SHORT_SHA=$(printf '%s' "$SHA" | cut -c1-12)

          # sha tag always gets pushed
          docker push "$REGISTRY/seshd:$SHORT_SHA"

          # branch tag only if the branch actually resolves cleanly
          BRANCH=$(sh .forgejo/scripts/resolve-branch.sh)
          echo "resolved branch: '$BRANCH'"
          case "$BRANCH" in
            main|develop)
              docker push "$REGISTRY/seshd:$BRANCH"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "skipping branch tag — branch '$BRANCH' is not main/develop"
              ;;
          esac

  # Publish the Helm chart to the OCI registry on every main/develop push
  # whose Chart.yaml version isn't already present. Versioning is manual
  # (bump `charts/akh-medu/Chart.yaml version:` in the same commit that
  # changes chart templates or values); CI just handles the publishing.
  #
  # Independent of docker-seshd so a broken image build doesn't hold back
  # a chart fix, and vice versa. Auth: same Solstice-populated docker
  # credentials as the image push — helm 3.8+ OCI uses the docker config.
  publish-chart:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - name: Install Helm
        run: |
          set -eu
          HELM_VERSION=v3.17.0
          curl -fsSL -o /tmp/helm.tgz "https://get.helm.sh/helm-${HELM_VERSION}-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
          tar -xzf /tmp/helm.tgz -C /tmp/
          sudo install -m755 /tmp/linux-amd64/helm /usr/local/bin/helm
          helm version --short

      - name: Package + publish chart to OCI
        run: |
          set -eu
          BRANCH=$(sh .forgejo/scripts/resolve-branch.sh)
          echo "detected branch: '$BRANCH'"
          case "$BRANCH" in
            main|develop) ;;
            *)
              echo "skipping chart publish — branch '$BRANCH' is not main/develop"
              exit 0
              ;;
          esac
          REGISTRY=oci://code.aopc.cloud/toasterson
          CHART_DIR=charts/akh-medu
          CHART_VERSION=$(awk '/^version:/ {print $2; exit}' "$CHART_DIR/Chart.yaml")
          if [ -z "$CHART_VERSION" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: could not read chart version from $CHART_DIR/Chart.yaml" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "chart version from Chart.yaml: $CHART_VERSION"

          # Idempotence: if this version is already up, log and exit clean.
          # `helm pull` against a missing version returns non-zero, against
          # an existing version succeeds and writes a .tgz into /tmp/check.
          mkdir -p /tmp/check
          if helm pull "$REGISTRY/akh-medu" --version "$CHART_VERSION" -d /tmp/check >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "chart akh-medu-$CHART_VERSION already published; nothing to do"
            exit 0
          fi

          # NOTE: we intentionally skip `helm dependency update` — the only
          # dependency is Bitnami postgresql (gated behind postgresql.enabled,
          # which is always false in production because we use the shared
          # CNPG postgres-ha cluster). Pulling from Docker Hub also risks
          # anonymous-pull rate-limits. If a future chart grows a dep that
          # must ship bundled, add it here.

          mkdir -p /tmp/pkg
          helm package "$CHART_DIR" -d /tmp/pkg
          helm push "/tmp/pkg/akh-medu-$CHART_VERSION.tgz" "$REGISTRY"
          echo "published akh-medu-$CHART_VERSION to $REGISTRY"

1	# Phase 31 — Skill Intelligence
2	
3	> Date: 2026-03-26
4	> Status: Planned
5	> Phase: 31
6	> Depends on: Phase 30 (procedural skills), Phase 26d (neural bridge),
7	>             Phase 28 (n akh router)
8	> ADR: [041-skill-intelligence](../decisions/041-skill-intelligence.md)
9	
10	## Motivation
11	
12	Phase 30 makes skills richer and easier to create. Phase 31 makes the skill
13	ecosystem self-organizing: skills discover themselves, load on demand, resolve
14	dependencies, share across instances, and bridge across domains.
15	
16	The end state: the agent is a learning system that acquires, organizes, and
17	deploys domain expertise autonomously — asking the user only for approval at
18	key decision points.
19	
20	## Sub-phases
21	
22	### 31a — Skill Dependency Graph (~400 lines)
23	
24	**Extend SkillManifest**:
25	```rust
26	pub depends: Vec<String>,        // Must be active before this skill
27	pub conflicts: Vec<String>,      // Cannot be co-active
28	pub provides: Vec<String>,       // Capability tags offered
29	pub requires: Vec<String>,       // Capability tags needed
30	```
31	
32	**Activation logic**:
33	1. Build dependency DAG (petgraph, reuse existing graph infrastructure)
34	2. Topological sort → activation order
35	3. Auto-activate prerequisites (recursive)
36	4. Reject if circular dependency or unresolvable conflict
37	5. Capability matching: find providers for `requires` tags
38	
39	**Deactivation**: Reverse topological order. Warn if dependents are still active.
40	
41	### 31b — Neural Skill Embeddings (~300 lines)
42	
43	Compute a prototype HyperVec per skill at activation time:
44	
45	```rust
46	fn compute_skill_prototype(engine: &Engine, skill_id: &str) -> AkhResult<HyperVec> {
47	    let triples = engine.triples_of_skill(skill_id)?;
48	    let vectors: Vec<HyperVec> = triples.iter()
49	        .flat_map(|t| [
50	            engine.item_memory().get_or_create(engine.ops(), t.subject),
51	            engine.item_memory().get_or_create(engine.ops(), t.predicate),
52	            engine.item_memory().get_or_create(engine.ops(), t.object),
53	        ])
54	        .collect();
55	    Ok(engine.ops().bundle(&vectors))
56	}
57	```
58	
59	Store prototype in ItemMemory with symbol `skill:proto:{skill_id}`.
60	
61	**Use cases**:
62	- Query→skill matching via similarity search
63	- Skill overlap detection (pairwise similarity matrix)
64	- n akh routing target selection
65	
66	### 31c — Skill-Aware Routing (~300 lines)
67	
68	Extend Phase 28's `n akh` router:
69	
70	```rust
71	// In NakhRouter::route():
72	// After feature extraction, before bandit selection:
73	
74	let query_vec = encode_label(ops, query_text);
75	let skill_matches = item_memory.search_prefix("skill:proto:", &query_vec, k=3)?;
76	
77	for matched_skill in skill_matches {
78	    if matched_skill.similarity > ACTIVATION_THRESHOLD {
79	        let skill_id = matched_skill.symbol.strip_prefix("skill:proto:");
80	        if skill_manager.state(skill_id) != SkillState::Hot {
81	            skill_manager.activate(skill_id)?;  // Lazy loading
82	        }
83	    }
84	}
85	```
86	
87	**Auto-deactivation**: Track last-used timestamp per skill. Idle task checks
88	for skills not used within cooldown period → deactivate to free memory.
89	
90	### 31d — Skill Discovery from Reasoning (~500 lines)
91	
92	**New module**: `src/skills/discover.rs`
93	
94	During background learning (sleep/consolidation), detect latent skills:
95	
96	```rust
97	pub struct SkillCandidate {
98	    pub suggested_name: String,
99	    pub domain_tags: Vec<String>,
100	    pub core_triples: Vec<Triple>,          // Connected subgraph
101	    pub related_rules: Vec<String>,         // Rules that fired within this subgraph
102	    pub related_actions: Vec<String>,       // Actions used in this domain
103	    pub discovery_provenance: ProvenanceId,
104	    pub confidence: f32,
105	}
106	```
107	
108	**Detection algorithm**:
109	1. During consolidation, identify clusters of frequently co-activated symbols
110	   (spreading activation patterns over last N cycles)
111	2. For each cluster, extract the induced subgraph from KG
112	3. Filter: must have ≥ threshold triples, ≥ 2 distinct predicates,
113	   coherent domain (prototype similarity within cluster > 0.6)
114	4. Check: is this already covered by an existing skill? (compare prototype
115	   against all skill prototypes)
116	5. If novel: LLM generates name + description, store as SkillCandidate
117	6. Present to user for approval
118	
119	**Idle task**: `discover_skills` runs during dream phase (Phase 11i),
120	piggybacks on the consolidation cycle.
121	
122	### 31e — Dynamic Skill Synthesis (~500 lines)
123	
124	**New module**: `src/skills/synthesis.rs`
125	
126	When the agent identifies a knowledge gap it cannot fill from existing skills:
127	
128	```rust
129	pub async fn synthesize_skill(
130	    engine: &Engine,
131	    gap: &KnowledgeGap,    // From directed curiosity (Phase 11j)
132	    author: &SkillAuthor,   // From Phase 30c
133	) -> SkillResult<SkillCandidate> {
134	    // 1. Use bootstrap ingestion to gather knowledge about the gap domain
135	    let sources = discover_resources(engine, &gap.domain, &gap.concepts)?;
136	    let ingested = ingest_resources(engine, &sources)?;
137	
138	    // 2. LLM-assisted authoring from ingested content
139	    let skill = author.author_from_triples(
140	        &gap.suggested_name,
141	        &ingested.triples,
142	        &gap.domain_tags,
143	    )?;
144	
145	    // 3. Return as candidate (user approval before activation)
146	    Ok(SkillCandidate::from_authored(skill, gap.provenance_id))

151	- Curiosity identifies information gaps
152	- If gap maps to a potential skill domain, trigger synthesis
153	- Synthesis uses existing bootstrap pipeline (web search, API, ingestion)
154	- Result is packaged as a skill via Phase 30c authoring

161	```rust

163	    // 1. Validate skill integrity (manifest + all referenced files exist)
164	    // 2. Compute content checksum (SHA-256)
165	    // 3. Create .akhskill archive (tar.gz)
166	    // 4. Include checksum in archive metadata
167	}

171	```rust

173	    // 1. Verify checksum
174	    // 2. Extract to temporary directory
175	    // 3. Validate manifest schema
176	    // 4. Check for conflicts with existing skills
177	    // 5. Move to skills_dir/{skill_id}/
178	    // 6. Return skill_id for activation

198	1. Compute pairwise similarity of skill prototypes
199	2. If similarity > OVERLAP_THRESHOLD (e.g., 0.55): flag as overlapping
200	3. Find shared symbols (symbols present in both skills' triple sets)
201	
202	**Bridge rule generation**:
203	- For shared symbols with different predicate contexts: generate disambiguation
204	  rules (e.g., "star" in astronomy vs. "star" in mythology)
205	- For complementary contexts: generate integration rules
206	  (e.g., physics velocity concept bridges to sports velocity concept)
207	- LLM assists: given two skill descriptions + shared concepts, generate

233	    pub expected_concepts: Vec<String>,  // Concepts the answer should reference
234	    pub bloom_level: BloomLevel,

236	```

238	**Integration with bootstrap** (Phase 14):
239	- When awakening with a skill-backed domain, use the skill's curriculum
240	  to order concept acquisition
241	- Assessment queries used by competence assessment (Phase 14, `competence.rs`)
242	  to measure progress

244	**LLM-assisted curriculum generation** (during Phase 30c authoring):
245	- When authoring a skill, LLM also generates a curriculum

1	# ADR 041 — Skill Intelligence: Self-Organizing Skill Ecosystem
2	
3	> Date: 2026-03-26
4	> Status: Proposed
5	> Phase: 31
6	> Depends on: Phase 30 (procedural skills), Phase 26d (neural bridge),
7	>             Phase 28 (n akh router)
8	> Enhances: Phase 27 (training data from skills), Phase 29b (skill exposure)
9	
10	## Context
11	
12	Phase 30 makes individual skills richer (procedural knowledge) and easier to
13	create (LLM-assisted authoring). Phase 31 addresses the ecosystem level:
14	how skills relate to each other, how they're discovered, how the engine
15	self-organizes its skill inventory.
16	
17	Currently:
18	- Skills are manually created and manually activated
19	- No dependency relationships between skills
20	- No way to discover that existing reasoning patterns should be packaged as skills
21	- No sharing mechanism beyond copying directories
22	- No awareness of which skills are relevant to a given query
23	- No cross-skill inference beyond shared KG triples
24	
25	## Decision
26	
27	### 1. Skill discovery from reasoning
28	
29	The agent already discovers facts during background learning (spreading
30	activation, sleep/dream phase, continuous learning). When it discovers a
31	cluster of related facts + inference patterns in a domain, it should
32	recognize this as a **latent skill** and offer to package it.
33	
34	**Trigger**: During background learning, if the consolidation phase identifies
35	N+ related triples (connected subgraph) with consistent provenance and high
36	usage, flag as skill candidate.
37	
38	**Process**:
39	1. Extract the connected subgraph of triples
40	2. Identify inference rules that fired within this subgraph
41	3. Identify action schemas that were used in this domain
42	4. LLM generates a skill name + description from the content
43	5. Store as `SkillCandidate` in KG (pending user approval)
44	6. User reviews and promotes to full skill
45	
46	### 2. Skill dependency graph
47	
48	Extend `SkillManifest` with:
49	```rust
50	pub depends: Vec<String>,           // Skill IDs that must be active first
51	pub conflicts: Vec<String>,         // Skill IDs that cannot be co-active
52	pub provides: Vec<String>,          // Capability tags this skill offers
53	pub requires: Vec<String>,          // Capability tags this skill needs
54	```
55	
56	**Activation**: Topological sort on dependency graph. Auto-activate
57	prerequisites. Reject activation if conflicts are detected.
58	
59	**Capability matching**: `provides`/`requires` enable loose coupling —
60	a skill says "I need spatial_reasoning" without naming a specific provider.
61	Multiple skills can provide the same capability (MoE selection).
62	
63	### 3. Neural skill embeddings
64	
65	Using Phase 26d's NeuralVsaBridge, create a **prototype HyperVec per skill**:
66	
67	- Bundle all of a skill's triple vectors into a single skill prototype
68	- Store in ItemMemory with a well-known `skill:prototype:{skill_id}` symbol
69	- Enable: "Which skill is most relevant to this query?" via similarity search
70	- Enable: "Which skills overlap?" via pairwise similarity
71	- Enable: "Which skill should I activate for this domain?" via n akh routing
72	
73	This is cheap — one extra HyperVec per skill, computed at activation time.
74	
75	### 4. Skill-aware routing (n akh integration)
76	
77	Extend Phase 28's `n akh` router with skill awareness:
78	
79	- Before routing a query, check similarity against skill prototypes
80	- If a relevant skill is Cold/Warm, auto-activate it (lazy loading)
81	- If multiple skills match, activate the one with highest quality score (Phase 30e)
82	- After query, if skill was auto-activated and isn't used again within
83	  cooldown period, auto-deactivate (memory conservation)
84	
85	This transforms skills from static, manually-managed knowledge packs into
86	**demand-loaded expertise modules**.
87	
88	### 5. Dynamic skill synthesis
89	
90	When the agent identifies a knowledge gap (directed curiosity, Phase 11j)
91	and can't find an existing skill:
92	
93	1. Agent recognizes gap: "I don't know how to reason about X"
94	2. Agent triggers bootstrap-style ingestion for domain X (web search, API)
95	3. Ingested knowledge is consolidated
96	4. LLM-assisted authoring (Phase 30c) packages the result as a new skill
97	5. New skill is activated and its quality tracked
98	
99	This closes the autonomy loop: the agent teaches itself by creating skills.
100	
101	### 6. Skill sharing protocol
102	
103	Skills are portable directories. A sharing protocol enables:
104	
105	**Export**: `akh skill export {name}` → produces a `.akhskill` archive
106	(tar.gz of the skill directory + integrity checksum)
107	
108	**Import**: `akh skill import {path}` → unpacks, validates manifest,
109	installs + activates
110	
111	**Registry** (future): A simple HTTP index where skills can be discovered
112	by domain tag, quality score, and compatibility version. Not a marketplace —
113	a FLOSS package registry like crates.io for skills.
114	
115	**Recipe integration**: Community recipes (Phase 14i) already reference
116	skillpacks by name. The sharing protocol provides the transport layer.
117	
118	### 7. Skill-to-skill inference
119	
120	Currently, triples from different skills coexist in the shared KG, enabling
121	implicit cross-skill inference via spreading activation. Make this explicit:
122	
123	**Bridge rules**: When two skills are co-active and share overlapping concepts
124	(detected via neural prototype similarity > threshold), generate bridge rules
125	that connect their ontologies.
126	
127	Example: "astronomy" skill has "star is-a celestial_body", "mythology" skill
128	has "star is-a symbol". Bridge rule: `(is_a ?x star) => (ambiguous ?x star)`
129	to flag the polysemy.
130	
131	**Cross-skill provenance**: When an inference chain crosses skill boundaries,
132	provenance records both source skills. Enables: "This conclusion combines
133	knowledge from astronomy and physics skills."
134	
135	### 8. Skill as curriculum
136	
137	Extend skills with a learning progression:
138	
139	```rust
140	pub struct SkillCurriculum {
141	    pub concepts: Vec<CurriculumConcept>,
142	    pub prerequisite_order: Vec<Vec<String>>,  // Topological layers
143	    pub bloom_levels: HashMap<String, BloomLevel>, // Concept → target mastery
144	    pub assessment_queries: Vec<String>,        // Questions to test understanding
145	}
146	```
147	
148	This connects to the bootstrap pipeline (Phase 14): when awakening in a new
149	domain, the skill's curriculum provides the learning path.
150	
151	## Consequences
152	
153	- SkillManifest extended with dependency/capability fields
154	- SkillManager gains auto-activation, dependency resolution, conflict detection
155	- New module: `src/skills/discover.rs` — latent skill detection
156	- New module: `src/skills/synthesis.rs` — dynamic skill creation from gap
157	- New module: `src/skills/share.rs` — export/import protocol
158	- New module: `src/skills/bridge.rs` — cross-skill inference rules
159	- Neural skill prototypes computed at activation (uses Phase 26d bridge)
160	- n akh router extended with skill-aware dispatch (uses Phase 28)
161	- Background idle task: skill candidate detection + quality monitoring
162	
163	## References
164	
165	- Phase 30: Procedural skills (format + authoring)
166	- Phase 26d: Neural→VSA bridge (skill embeddings)
167	- Phase 28: n akh semantic router (skill-aware routing)
168	- Phase 11j: Directed curiosity (knowledge gap detection)
169	- Phase 14i: Community recipes (skill sharing)
170	- Phase 29b: Skill exposure (user-facing controls)
171

**Priority:** 31a (dependencies) → 31b (embeddings) → 31c (routing) → 31f (sharing) → 31d (discovery) → 31e (synthesis) → 31g (cross-skill) → 31h (curriculum)

### 6. ADR 041 — Skill Intelligence

**Status:** Proposed (March 2026)  
**Phases:** 30, 26d, 28, 11j, 14, 14i (dependencies)

**8 Key Decisions:**

1. **Skill discovery from reasoning** - detect latent skills during consolidation
2. **Skill dependency graph** - DAG with topological activation
3. **Neural skill embeddings** - HyperVec prototypes for similarity matching
4. **Skill-aware routing** - lazy load skills based on query similarity
5. **Dynamic synthesis** - create skills from knowledge gaps (curiosity-driven)
6. **Sharing protocol** - `.akhskill` archives with CRC-32 integrity
7. **Skill-to-skill inference** - bridge rules for overlapping concepts
8. **Skills as curriculum** - Bloom-based learning progression

**Impact:** Self-organizing skill ecosystem, autonomous knowledge acquisition, community skill registry.

### 7. src/skills/manager.rs - Full Analysis

**Key Struct: SkillManager**
- `skills_dir: PathBuf` - location of skill directories
- `skills: RwLock<HashMap<String, LoadedSkill>>` - all known skills
- `loaded_bytes: AtomicUsize` - memory tracker
- `max_bytes: usize` - memory budget
- `rule_sources: RwLock<HashMap<String, Vec<(String, String, String)>>>` - egg rules per skill
- `skill_triples: RwLock<HashMap<String, Vec<Triple>>>` - triples per skill (Phase 31b)
- `prototypes: DashMap<String, Vec<u8>>` - serialized HyperVecs (Phase 31b)
- `last_used: DashMap<String, Instant>` - timestamp tracking (Phase 31c)

**Lifecycle Methods:**
- `discover()` - scan directory, register as Cold
- `warm(skill_id)` - parse manifest, transition to Warm
- `activate(skill_id, knowledge_graph)` - load triples/rules, transition to Hot, check conflicts (31a), record last-used (31c)
- `deactivate(skill_id)` - unload, free memory, clear prototypes/last_used
- `skill_state(skill_id)` - check current state
- `hot_activation(skill_id)` - get activation summary for already-active skill

**Phase 31b Methods:**
- `triples_of_skill(skill_id)` - retrieve stored triple set
- `compute_and_store_prototype(skill_id, ops)` - bundle triple symbol vectors into HyperVec
- `prototype_bytes(skill_id)` - retrieve serialized prototype
- `prototype(skill_id)` - deserialize and return HyperVec
- `match_skills_to_query(query, ops, k, threshold)` - find k most similar skills to query vector

**Phase 31c Methods:**
- `touch_skill(skill_id)` - update last-used timestamp
- `collect_idle_skills(cooldown)` - find skills not used within cooldown period
- `active_skill_ids()` - list all Hot skills

**Phase 31a Methods:**
- `all_manifests()` - get all skill manifests (for graph construction)
- `activation_plan(target_skill_id)` - compute ordered list of skills to activate (dependencies first)

**Utilities:**
- `list()` - all skills with state/domains/counts
- `get_info(skill_id)` - detailed info for one skill
- `active_rules()` - compile all Hot skill rules into egg Rewrites
- `add_triple_count(skill_id, extra)` - increment triple counter

**Testing:**
- 14 tests covering: discovery, warming, activation, budget enforcement, deactivation, prototype computation, idle detection, conflict prevention

### 8. src/skills/mod.rs - Type Definitions

**Public Types Exported:**

1. **SkillState (enum)** - Cold | Warm | Hot
2. **SkillManifest (struct)** - Skill metadata
   - id, name, version, description
   - domains: Vec<String> (e.g., "astronomy", "linguistics")
   - weight_size_bytes: u64
   - triples_file, rules_file, cli_tools, wasm_tools: paths
   - tool_config: HashMap for tool parameters
   - Phase 31a: depends, conflicts, provides, requires
   - Phase 31f: remote_url
   - Phase 31h: curriculum_file

3. **LoadedSkill (struct)** - manifest + state + metrics
   - manifest: SkillManifest
   - state: SkillState
   - triple_count, rule_count, memory_bytes: usize
   - last_used_at: Option<Instant> (Phase 31c)

4. **SkillInfo (struct)** - summary for listing
   - id, name, version, description, state, domains
   - triple_count, rule_count
   - provide, requires

5. **SkillActivation (struct)** - activation result
   - skill_id, triples_loaded, rules_loaded, memory_bytes

6. **SkillInstallPayload (struct)** - remote install request
   - manifest: SkillManifest
   - triples: Vec<LabelTriple> (label-based)
   - rules: String

7. **LabelTriple (struct)** - label-based triple for ingestion
   - subject, predicate, object: String
   - confidence: f32 (default 1.0)

8. **SkillResultType<T>** - type alias for SkillResult<T>

### 9. src/main.rs - CLI Overview

**Structure:** ~235K bytes, large CLI with 40+ subcommands

**Major Command Groups:**
- `workspace` - manage workspaces
- `skill` - manage skillpacks (load, activate, export, import, list)
- `ingest` - load triples (JSON, CSV, text)
- `render` - show knowledge in glyph notation
- `agent` - run autonomous agent
- `pim` - personal info management
- `cal` - calendar operations
- `pref` - preference learning
- `causal` - causal reasoning
- `awaken` - identity/bootstrap
- `seed` - knowledge packs
- `chat` - interactive TUI chat
- `library` - shared content library
- `service` - macOS service management
- `setup` - NLU model download
- `wiki` - Akhipedia (knowledge wiki)

**Global Options:**
- `--data-dir` - override data directory
- `-w, --workspace` - workspace name (default "default")
- `--dimension` - hypervector dimension (default 10000)
- `--language` - parser language (en, ru, ar, fr, es, auto)

### 10. src/error.rs - Error System

**Architecture:** Top-level `AkhError` enum that wraps subsystem-specific errors

**Error Variants (61 total):**
- VsaError (4 variants) - hypervector operations
- StoreError (5) - persistence layer
- GraphError (4) - knowledge graph
- SymbolError (4) - symbol management
- InferError (3) - inference engine
- ReasonError (9) - symbolic reasoning
- **SkillError (11) - skill management**
- ProvenanceError (3) - provenance tracking
- PipelineError (4) - data pipelines
- EngineError (3) - engine configuration
- Plus 20+ other subsystems

**SkillError Variants (11):**
1. `NotFound { name }` - skill not registered
2. `LoadError { message }` - disk load failure
3. `MemoryBudgetExceeded { required_mb, available_mb }` - OOM
4. `InvalidManifest { path, message }` - malformed skill.json
5. `InvalidRule { skill_id, message }` - egg rule parse failure
6. `InvalidTransition { skill_id, from, to }` - lifecycle violation
7. `NoSkillsDir { path }` - missing skills directory
8. `Io { skill_id, source }` - filesystem error
9. `CircularDependency { cycle }` - cyclic dependency in DAG
10. `SkillConflict { skill_id, conflict }` - conflicting active skills
11. `UnresolvedCapability { capability }` - no provider for capability
12. `ArchiveError { message }` - .akhskill creation/unpacking failure
13. `ChecksumMismatch { expected, actual }` - archive tampering detected

**Each error includes:**
- Diagnostic code (e.g., `akh::skill::not_found`)
- Help text with remediation steps
- Optional source chain

**Result Type Aliases:**
- `AkhResult<T>` - top-level error
- `SkillResult<T>` - skill subsystem specific

---

## Summary

The **akh-medu** project is a comprehensive neuro-symbolic AI engine implementing a sophisticated skill management system (Phase 31) on top of a knowledge graph, vector symbolic architecture (VSA), and symbolic reasoning engine. The skills subsystem provides:

- **Lifecycle Management:** Cold → Warm → Hot skill states with memory budgeting
- **Dependency Resolution:** Topological DAG with capability matching (Phase 31a)
- **Neural Integration:** HyperVec prototypes for semantic skill matching (Phase 31b)
- **Smart Routing:** Lazy-loading skills based on query similarity (Phase 31c)
- **Autonomous Discovery:** Detect latent skills from background reasoning patterns (Phase 31d)
- **Dynamic Synthesis:** Create skills from knowledge gaps (Phase 31e)
- **Portability:** Export/import via `.akhskill` archives with CRC-32 integrity (Phase 31f)
- **Cross-Skill Inference:** Bridge rules for overlapping concepts (Phase 31g)
- **Learning Progression:** Bloom-taxonomy-based curriculum (Phase 31h)

The codebase is well-architected with comprehensive error handling, extensive testing, and clear module boundaries. The implementation is production-ready with proper memory management, concurrency control (DashMap), and persistence via redb.

## Summary

The **akh-medu** project is a comprehensive neuro-symbolic AI engine implementing a sophisticated skill management system (Phase 31) on top of a knowledge graph, vector symbolic architecture (VSA), and symbolic reasoning engine. The skills subsystem provides:

- **Lifecycle Management:** Cold → Warm → Hot skill states with memory budgeting
- **Dependency Resolution:** Topological DAG with capability matching (Phase 31a)
- **Neural Integration:** HyperVec prototypes for semantic skill matching (Phase 31b)
- **Smart Routing:** Lazy-loading skills based on query similarity (Phase 31c)
- **Autonomous Discovery:** Detect latent skills from background reasoning patterns (Phase 31d)
- **Dynamic Synthesis:** Create skills from knowledge gaps (Phase 31e)
- **Portability:** Export/import via `.akhskill` archives with CRC-32 integrity (Phase 31f)
- **Cross-Skill Inference:** Bridge rules for overlapping concepts (Phase 31g)
- **Learning Progression:** Bloom-taxonomy-based curriculum (Phase 31h)

The codebase is well-architected with comprehensive error handling, extensive testing, and clear module boundaries. The implementation is production-ready with proper memory management, concurrency control (DashMap), and persistence via redb.

19	    /// Use information in new situations.
20	    Apply,
21	    /// Draw connections among ideas.
22	    Analyze,
23	    /// Justify a decision or course of action.
24	    Evaluate,
25	    /// Produce new or original work.
26	    Create,
27	}
28	
29	impl std::fmt::Display for BloomLevel {
30	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
31	        let s = match self {
32	            Self::Remember => "remember",
33	            Self::Understand => "understand",
34	            Self::Apply => "apply",
35	            Self::Analyze => "analyze",
36	            Self::Evaluate => "evaluate",
37	            Self::Create => "create",
38	        };
39	        write!(f, "{s}")
40	    }
41	}
42	
43	impl std::str::FromStr for BloomLevel {
44	    type Err = String;
45	    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
46	        match s.to_lowercase().as_str() {
47	            "remember" => Ok(Self::Remember),
48	            "understand" => Ok(Self::Understand),
49	            "apply" => Ok(Self::Apply),
50	            "analyze" | "analyse" => Ok(Self::Analyze),

1	# Phase 31 — Skill Intelligence
2	
3	> Date: 2026-03-26
4	> Status: Planned
5	> Phase: 31
6	> Depends on: Phase 30 (procedural skills), Phase 26d (neural bridge),
7	>             Phase 28 (n akh router)
8	> ADR: [041-skill-intelligence](../decisions/041-skill-intelligence.md)
9	
10	## Motivation
11	
12	Phase 30 makes skills richer and easier to create. Phase 31 makes the skill
13	ecosystem self-organizing: skills discover themselves, load on demand, resolve
14	dependencies, share across instances, and bridge across domains.
15	
16	The end state: the agent is a learning system that acquires, organizes, and
17	deploys domain expertise autonomously — asking the user only for approval at
18	key decision points.
19	
20	## Sub-phases
21	
22	### 31a — Skill Dependency Graph (~400 lines)
23	
24	**Extend SkillManifest**:
25	```rust
26	pub depends: Vec<String>,        // Must be active before this skill
27	pub conflicts: Vec<String>,      // Cannot be co-active
28	pub provides: Vec<String>,       // Capability tags offered
29	pub requires: Vec<String>,       // Capability tags needed
30	```
31	
32	**Activation logic**:
33	1. Build dependency DAG (petgraph, reuse existing graph infrastructure)
34	2. Topological sort → activation order
35	3. Auto-activate prerequisites (recursive)
36	4. Reject if circular dependency or unresolvable conflict
37	5. Capability matching: find providers for `requires` tags
38	
39	**Deactivation**: Reverse topological order. Warn if dependents are still active.
40	
41	### 31b — Neural Skill Embeddings (~300 lines)
42	
43	Compute a prototype HyperVec per skill at activation time:
44	
45	```rust
46	fn compute_skill_prototype(engine: &Engine, skill_id: &str) -> AkhResult<HyperVec> {
47	    let triples = engine.triples_of_skill(skill_id)?;
48	    let vectors: Vec<HyperVec> = triples.iter()
49	        .flat_map(|t| [
50	            engine.item_memory().get_or_create(engine.ops(), t.subject),
51	            engine.item_memory().get_or_create(engine.ops(), t.predicate),
52	            engine.item_memory().get_or_create(engine.ops(), t.object),
53	        ])
54	        .collect();
55	    Ok(engine.ops().bundle(&vectors))
56	}
57	```
58	
59	Store prototype in ItemMemory with symbol `skill:proto:{skill_id}`.
60	
61	**Use cases**:
62	- Query→skill matching via similarity search
63	- Skill overlap detection (pairwise similarity matrix)
64	- n akh routing target selection
65	
66	### 31c — Skill-Aware Routing (~300 lines)
67	
68	Extend Phase 28's `n akh` router:
69	
70	```rust
71	// In NakhRouter::route():
72	// After feature extraction, before bandit selection:
73	
74	let query_vec = encode_label(ops, query_text);
75	let skill_matches = item_memory.search_prefix("skill:proto:", &query_vec, k=3)?;
76	
77	for matched_skill in skill_matches {
78	    if matched_skill.similarity > ACTIVATION_THRESHOLD {
79	        let skill_id = matched_skill.symbol.strip_prefix("skill:proto:");
80	        if skill_manager.state(skill_id) != SkillState::Hot {
81	            skill_manager.activate(skill_id)?;  // Lazy loading
82	        }
83	    }
84	}
85	```
86	
87	**Auto-deactivation**: Track last-used timestamp per skill. Idle task checks
88	for skills not used within cooldown period → deactivate to free memory.
89	
90	### 31d — Skill Discovery from Reasoning (~500 lines)
91	
92	**New module**: `src/skills/discover.rs`
93	
94	During background learning (sleep/consolidation), detect latent skills:
95	
96	```rust
97	pub struct SkillCandidate {
98	    pub suggested_name: String,
99	    pub domain_tags: Vec<String>,
100	    pub core_triples: Vec<Triple>,          // Connected subgraph
101	    pub related_rules: Vec<String>,         // Rules that fired within this subgraph
102	    pub related_actions: Vec<String>,       // Actions used in this domain
103	    pub discovery_provenance: ProvenanceId,
104	    pub confidence: f32,
105	}
106	```
107	
108	**Detection algorithm**:
109	1. During consolidation, identify clusters of frequently co-activated symbols
110	   (spreading activation patterns over last N cycles)
111	2. For each cluster, extract the induced subgraph from KG
112	3. Filter: must have ≥ threshold triples, ≥ 2 distinct predicates,
113	   coherent domain (prototype similarity within cluster > 0.6)
114	4. Check: is this already covered by an existing skill? (compare prototype
115	   against all skill prototypes)
116	5. If novel: LLM generates name + description, store as SkillCandidate
117	6. Present to user for approval
118	
119	**Idle task**: `discover_skills` runs during dream phase (Phase 11i),
120	piggybacks on the consolidation cycle.
121	
122	### 31e — Dynamic Skill Synthesis (~500 lines)
123	
124	**New module**: `src/skills/synthesis.rs`
125	
126	When the agent identifies a knowledge gap it cannot fill from existing skills:
127	
128	```rust
129	pub async fn synthesize_skill(
130	    engine: &Engine,
131	    gap: &KnowledgeGap,    // From directed curiosity (Phase 11j)
132	    author: &SkillAuthor,   // From Phase 30c
133	) -> SkillResult<SkillCandidate> {
134	    // 1. Use bootstrap ingestion to gather knowledge about the gap domain
135	    let sources = discover_resources(engine, &gap.domain, &gap.concepts)?;
136	    let ingested = ingest_resources(engine, &sources)?;
137	
138	    // 2. LLM-assisted authoring from ingested content
139	    let skill = author.author_from_triples(
140	        &gap.suggested_name,
141	        &ingested.triples,
142	        &gap.domain_tags,
143	    )?;
144	
145	    // 3. Return as candidate (user approval before activation)
146	    Ok(SkillCandidate::from_authored(skill, gap.provenance_id))
147	}
148	```
149	
150	**Integration with directed curiosity** (Phase 11j):
151	- Curiosity identifies information gaps
152	- If gap maps to a potential skill domain, trigger synthesis
153	- Synthesis uses existing bootstrap pipeline (web search, API, ingestion)
154	- Result is packaged as a skill via Phase 30c authoring
155	
156	### 31f — Skill Sharing Protocol (~400 lines)
157	
158	**New module**: `src/skills/share.rs`
159	
160	**Export**:
161	```rust
162	pub fn export_skill(skill_dir: &Path, output: &Path) -> SkillResult<PathBuf> {
163	    // 1. Validate skill integrity (manifest + all referenced files exist)
164	    // 2. Compute content checksum (SHA-256)
165	    // 3. Create .akhskill archive (tar.gz)
166	    // 4. Include checksum in archive metadata
167	}
168	```
169	
170	**Import**:
171	```rust
172	pub fn import_skill(archive: &Path, skills_dir: &Path) -> SkillResult<String> {
173	    // 1. Verify checksum
174	    // 2. Extract to temporary directory
175	    // 3. Validate manifest schema
176	    // 4. Check for conflicts with existing skills
177	    // 5. Move to skills_dir/{skill_id}/
178	    // 6. Return skill_id for activation
179	}
180	```
181	
182	**CLI**: `akh skill export {name} -o path.akhskill`
183	        `akh skill import path.akhskill`
184	
185	**Recipe integration**: Recipes can reference remote skill URLs:
186	```toml
187	[resources]
188	skillpacks = ["local:astronomy", "https://skills.example.com/physics-v2.akhskill"]
189	```
190	
191	### 31g — Cross-Skill Inference (~400 lines)
192	
193	**New module**: `src/skills/bridge.rs`
194	
195	When multiple skills are co-active, detect and handle concept overlap:
196	
197	**Overlap detection** (at activation time):
198	1. Compute pairwise similarity of skill prototypes
199	2. If similarity > OVERLAP_THRESHOLD (e.g., 0.55): flag as overlapping
200	3. Find shared symbols (symbols present in both skills' triple sets)
201	
202	**Bridge rule generation**:
203	- For shared symbols with different predicate contexts: generate disambiguation
204	  rules (e.g., "star" in astronomy vs. "star" in mythology)
205	- For complementary contexts: generate integration rules
206	  (e.g., physics velocity concept bridges to sports velocity concept)
207	- LLM assists: given two skill descriptions + shared concepts, generate
208	  appropriate bridge rules
209	- Bridge rules tagged with `DerivationKind::SkillBridge { source_skills }`
210	
211	**Cross-skill provenance**: When an inference chain traverses triples from
212	multiple skills, provenance records all contributing skills.
213	
214	### 31h — Skill Curriculum (~300 lines)
215	
216	Extend skills with a learning progression for bootstrapping:
217	
218	```rust
219	pub struct SkillCurriculum {
220	    pub concepts: Vec<CurriculumConcept>,
221	    pub layers: Vec<Vec<String>>,        // Topological layers (learn in order)
222	    pub assessments: Vec<Assessment>,
223	}
224	
225	pub struct CurriculumConcept {
226	    pub name: String,
227	    pub bloom_target: BloomLevel,        // Remember, Understand, Apply, etc.
228	    pub prerequisites: Vec<String>,
229	}
230	
231	pub struct Assessment {
232	    pub query: String,                   // Question to test understanding
233	    pub expected_concepts: Vec<String>,  // Concepts the answer should reference
234	    pub bloom_level: BloomLevel,
235	}
236	```
237	
238	**Integration with bootstrap** (Phase 14):
239	- When awakening with a skill-backed domain, use the skill's curriculum
240	  to order concept acquisition
241	- Assessment queries used by competence assessment (Phase 14, `competence.rs`)
242	  to measure progress
243	
244	**LLM-assisted curriculum generation** (during Phase 30c authoring):
245	- When authoring a skill, LLM also generates a curriculum
246	- Curriculum stored as `curriculum.json` in skill directory
247	
248	## Estimated Effort
249	
250	| Sub-phase | Lines | Complexity | Dependencies |
251	|---|---|---|---|
252	| 31a — Dependency graph | ~400 | Medium | None (schema) |
253	| 31b — Neural embeddings | ~300 | Low | Phase 26d |
254	| 31c — Skill-aware routing | ~300 | Medium | Phase 28, 31b |
255	| 31d — Discovery from reasoning | ~500 | High | Phase 30c, 31b |
256	| 31e — Dynamic synthesis | ~500 | High | Phase 30c, 11j |
257	| 31f — Sharing protocol | ~400 | Low | None |
258	| 31g — Cross-skill inference | ~400 | High | Phase 26b, 31b |
259	| 31h — Skill curriculum | ~300 | Medium | Phase 14 |
260	| **Total** | **~3,100** | | |
261	
262	## Priority Order
263	
264	1. **31a — Dependencies** (foundational, enables safe multi-skill activation)
265	2. **31b — Neural embeddings** (enables 31c, 31d, 31g)
266	3. **31c — Skill-aware routing** (biggest UX impact: automatic expertise loading)
267	4. **31f — Sharing protocol** (enables community ecosystem)
268	5. **31d — Discovery** (autonomy: agent finds its own skills)
269	6. **31e — Synthesis** (autonomy: agent creates skills from gaps)
270	7. **31g — Cross-skill inference** (quality: multi-domain reasoning)
271	8. **31h — Curriculum** (bootstrap enhancement)
272

1	# ADR 041 — Skill Intelligence: Self-Organizing Skill Ecosystem
2	
3	> Date: 2026-03-26
4	> Status: Proposed
5	> Phase: 31
6	> Depends on: Phase 30 (procedural skills), Phase 26d (neural bridge),
7	>             Phase 28 (n akh router)
8	> Enhances: Phase 27 (training data from skills), Phase 29b (skill exposure)
9	
10	## Context
11	
12	Phase 30 makes individual skills richer (procedural knowledge) and easier to
13	create (LLM-assisted authoring). Phase 31 addresses the ecosystem level:
14	how skills relate to each other, how they're discovered, how the engine
15	self-organizes its skill inventory.
16	
17	Currently:
18	- Skills are manually created and manually activated
19	- No dependency relationships between skills
20	- No way to discover that existing reasoning patterns should be packaged as skills
21	- No sharing mechanism beyond copying directories
22	- No awareness of which skills are relevant to a given query
23	- No cross-skill inference beyond shared KG triples
24	
25	## Decision
26	
27	### 1. Skill discovery from reasoning
28	
29	The agent already discovers facts during background learning (spreading
30	activation, sleep/dream phase, continuous learning). When it discovers a
31	cluster of related facts + inference patterns in a domain, it should
32	recognize this as a **latent skill** and offer to package it.
33	
34	**Trigger**: During background learning, if the consolidation phase identifies
35	N+ related triples (connected subgraph) with consistent provenance and high
36	usage, flag as skill candidate.
37	
38	**Process**:
39	1. Extract the connected subgraph of triples
40	2. Identify inference rules that fired within this subgraph
41	3. Identify action schemas that were used in this domain
42	4. LLM generates a skill name + description from the content
43	5. Store as `SkillCandidate` in KG (pending user approval)
44	6. User reviews and promotes to full skill
45	
46	### 2. Skill dependency graph
47	
48	Extend `SkillManifest` with:
49	```rust
50	pub depends: Vec<String>,           // Skill IDs that must be active first
51	pub conflicts: Vec<String>,         // Skill IDs that cannot be co-active
52	pub provides: Vec<String>,          // Capability tags this skill offers
53	pub requires: Vec<String>,          // Capability tags this skill needs
54	```
55	
56	**Activation**: Topological sort on dependency graph. Auto-activate
57	prerequisites. Reject activation if conflicts are detected.
58	
59	**Capability matching**: `provides`/`requires` enable loose coupling —
60	a skill says "I need spatial_reasoning" without naming a specific provider.
61	Multiple skills can provide the same capability (MoE selection).
62	
63	### 3. Neural skill embeddings
64	
65	Using Phase 26d's NeuralVsaBridge, create a **prototype HyperVec per skill**:
66	
67	- Bundle all of a skill's triple vectors into a single skill prototype
68	- Store in ItemMemory with a well-known `skill:prototype:{skill_id}` symbol
69	- Enable: "Which skill is most relevant to this query?" via similarity search
70	- Enable: "Which skills overlap?" via pairwise similarity
71	- Enable: "Which skill should I activate for this domain?" via n akh routing
72	
73	This is cheap — one extra HyperVec per skill, computed at activation time.
74	
75	### 4. Skill-aware routing (n akh integration)
76	
77	Extend Phase 28's `n akh` router with skill awareness:
78	
79	- Before routing a query, check similarity against skill prototypes
80	- If a relevant skill is Cold/Warm, auto-activate it (lazy loading)
81	- If multiple skills match, activate the one with highest quality score (Phase 30e)
82	- After query, if skill was auto-activated and isn't used again within
83	  cooldown period, auto-deactivate (memory conservation)
84	
85	This transforms skills from static, manually-managed knowledge packs into
86	**demand-loaded expertise modules**.
87	
88	### 5. Dynamic skill synthesis
89	
90	When the agent identifies a knowledge gap (directed curiosity, Phase 11j)
91	and can't find an existing skill:
92	
93	1. Agent recognizes gap: "I don't know how to reason about X"
94	2. Agent triggers bootstrap-style ingestion for domain X (web search, API)
95	3. Ingested knowledge is consolidated
96	4. LLM-assisted authoring (Phase 30c) packages the result as a new skill
97	5. New skill is activated and its quality tracked
98	
99	This closes the autonomy loop: the agent teaches itself by creating skills.
100	
101	### 6. Skill sharing protocol
102	
103	Skills are portable directories. A sharing protocol enables:
104	
105	**Export**: `akh skill export {name}` → produces a `.akhskill` archive
106	(tar.gz of the skill directory + integrity checksum)
107	
108	**Import**: `akh skill import {path}` → unpacks, validates manifest,
109	installs + activates
110	
111	**Registry** (future): A simple HTTP index where skills can be discovered
112	by domain tag, quality score, and compatibility version. Not a marketplace —
113	a FLOSS package registry like crates.io for skills.
114	
115	**Recipe integration**: Community recipes (Phase 14i) already reference
116	skillpacks by name. The sharing protocol provides the transport layer.
117	
118	### 7. Skill-to-skill inference
119	
120	Currently, triples from different skills coexist in the shared KG, enabling
121	implicit cross-skill inference via spreading activation. Make this explicit:
122	
123	**Bridge rules**: When two skills are co-active and share overlapping concepts
124	(detected via neural prototype similarity > threshold), generate bridge rules
125	that connect their ontologies.
126	
127	Example: "astronomy" skill has "star is-a celestial_body", "mythology" skill
128	has "star is-a symbol". Bridge rule: `(is_a ?x star) => (ambiguous ?x star)`
129	to flag the polysemy.
130	
131	**Cross-skill provenance**: When an inference chain crosses skill boundaries,
132	provenance records both source skills. Enables: "This conclusion combines
133	knowledge from astronomy and physics skills."
134	
135	### 8. Skill as curriculum
136	
137	Extend skills with a learning progression:
138	
139	```rust
140	pub struct SkillCurriculum {
141	    pub concepts: Vec<CurriculumConcept>,
142	    pub prerequisite_order: Vec<Vec<String>>,  // Topological layers
143	    pub bloom_levels: HashMap<String, BloomLevel>, // Concept → target mastery
144	    pub assessment_queries: Vec<String>,        // Questions to test understanding
145	}
146	```
147	
148	This connects to the bootstrap pipeline (Phase 14): when awakening in a new
149	domain, the skill's curriculum provides the learning path.
150	
151	## Consequences
152	
153	- SkillManifest extended with dependency/capability fields
154	- SkillManager gains auto-activation, dependency resolution, conflict detection
155	- New module: `src/skills/discover.rs` — latent skill detection
156	- New module: `src/skills/synthesis.rs` — dynamic skill creation from gap
157	- New module: `src/skills/share.rs` — export/import protocol
158	- New module: `src/skills/bridge.rs` — cross-skill inference rules
159	- Neural skill prototypes computed at activation (uses Phase 26d bridge)
160	- n akh router extended with skill-aware dispatch (uses Phase 28)
161	- Background idle task: skill candidate detection + quality monitoring
162	
163	## References
164	
165	- Phase 30: Procedural skills (format + authoring)
166	- Phase 26d: Neural→VSA bridge (skill embeddings)
167	- Phase 28: n akh semantic router (skill-aware routing)
168	- Phase 11j: Directed curiosity (knowledge gap detection)
169	- Phase 14i: Community recipes (skill sharing)
170	- Phase 29b: Skill exposure (user-facing controls)
171

1	//! Skill discovery from reasoning: detect latent skills in background learning.
2	//!
3	//! Phase 31d — during the background consolidation cycle (sleep/dream phase),
4	//! identify clusters of frequently co-activated symbols that form a coherent
5	//! domain. When a cluster meets the novelty and coherence thresholds, it is
6	//! surfaced as a `SkillCandidate` for user review and optional promotion to a
7	//! full skillpack.
8	
9	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
10	
11	use crate::graph::Triple;
12	use crate::symbol::SymbolId;
13	
14	/// A cluster of co-activated symbols discovered during background reasoning.
15	///
16	/// This is the raw signal from spreading-activation tracking; further analysis
17	/// may refine it into a `SkillCandidate`.
18	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
19	pub struct CoActivationCluster {
20	    /// Symbol IDs that were frequently activated together.
21	    pub symbols: Vec<SymbolId>,
22	    /// Estimated co-activation frequency (higher = stronger cluster).
23	    pub frequency: f32,
24	    /// Triples induced by these symbols in the knowledge graph.
25	    pub induced_triples: Vec<Triple>,
26	}
27	
28	/// Configuration for the skill candidate detection pass.
29	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
30	pub struct DiscoveryConfig {
31	    /// Minimum number of triples in the induced subgraph for a cluster to be
32	    /// considered a skill candidate.
33	    pub min_triples: usize,
34	    /// Minimum number of distinct predicates required (tests conceptual diversity).
35	    pub min_distinct_predicates: usize,
36	    /// Minimum intra-cluster prototype similarity for coherence check (0.0–1.0).
37	    pub min_coherence: f32,
38	    /// Minimum co-activation frequency threshold to consider a cluster.
39	    pub min_frequency: f32,
40	    /// Prototype similarity threshold against existing skills: if any existing
41	    /// skill prototype is more similar than this, the cluster is not novel.
42	    pub novelty_threshold: f32,
43	}
44	
45	impl Default for DiscoveryConfig {
46	    fn default() -> Self {
47	        Self {
48	            min_triples: 5,
49	            min_distinct_predicates: 2,
50	            min_coherence: 0.55,
51	            min_frequency: 3.0,
52	            novelty_threshold: 0.70,
53	        }
54	    }
55	}

57	/// A candidate skill surfaced from background reasoning.
58	///
59	/// Candidates are stored in the KG and presented to the user for review.
60	/// A user-approved candidate can be packaged into a full skillpack via the
61	/// Phase 30c authoring pipeline.
62	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
63	pub struct SkillCandidate {
64	    /// LLM-suggested name for the potential skill (pending user review).
65	    pub suggested_name: String,
66	    /// LLM-suggested description.
67	    pub suggested_description: String,
68	    /// Domain tags inferred from the cluster.
69	    pub domain_tags: Vec<String>,
70	    /// Core triples that define the candidate skill's content.
71	    pub core_triples: Vec<Triple>,
72	    /// Egg rewrite rules that fired within this cluster's subgraph.
73	    pub related_rules: Vec<String>,
74	    /// Confidence that this is a genuinely useful, novel skill (0.0–1.0).
75	    pub confidence: f32,
76	    /// Opaque provenance token (e.g., a SymbolId or UUID string) linking back
77	    /// to the consolidation event that surfaced this candidate.
78	    pub provenance_token: String,
79	}
80	
81	/// Filter: check whether a co-activation cluster meets the minimum quality
82	/// thresholds from `config` to be considered for skill candidate promotion.
83	pub fn meets_quality_threshold(cluster: &CoActivationCluster, config: &DiscoveryConfig) -> bool {
84	    if cluster.frequency < config.min_frequency {
85	        return false;
86	    }
87	    if cluster.induced_triples.len() < config.min_triples {
88	        return false;
89	    }
90	    let distinct_predicates: std::collections::HashSet<SymbolId> = cluster
91	        .induced_triples
92	        .iter()
93	        .map(|t| t.predicate)
94	        .collect();
95	    if distinct_predicates.len() < config.min_distinct_predicates {
96	        return false;
97	    }
98	    true
99	}
